mainTopic: Removing the טומאה status of food handles by action, and whether boards may be used as סכך (the dispute of רב and שמואל)
overview: The עמוד finishes a challenge from the previous עמוד. Thought can make an item able to receive טומאה, but only an action can remove that status. So how can the רבנן allow grain stalks harvested for food as סכך? The גמרא answers that the stalks were actually trampled (בססן), which is a real action. אחרים forbid them because they follow רבי יוסי, who says trampled handles stay טמא. They stay טמא because they are still useful: on the threshing floor for a pitchfork, and on a סוכה for holding the grain when taking the roof down. רבי אלעזר then compares the prayer of צדיקים to a pitchfork (עתר) that turns ה׳ from harshness to mercy. A new משנה follows: רבי יהודה allows boards as סכך and רבי מאיר forbids them. רב and שמואל disagree about which board widths that dispute covers. The עמוד ends as the גמרא begins a new proof from two sheets that combine, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Thought brings into impurity, but only action takes out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a rule about כלים: thought can make an item susceptible to טומאה, but only a physical change can remove that status. This challenges the רבנן, who seem to let intention alone remove the status of food handles.
steps.simpleTranslation: Vessels go down into impurity through thought, but they only come up from their impurity through a change made by action. Action cancels a status made by action and a status made by thought. Thought cancels neither a status made by action nor a status made by thought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing a quote that began on the previous עמוד. It uses this quote to challenge the view of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is lopsided. Deciding to use an item can make it a כלי that receives טומאה, but deciding to stop using it does nothing until you physically change it. The רבנן seem to say that intent to use the stalks as סכך cancels the handles' status, which would mean thought undoes a status. That contradicts this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Thought or intention
A change made by a physical action
They 'go down' into a state of being able to become impure
They 'come up' out of that impure status

steps.confusionAlert: This quote does not start here. Its opening words (that all כלים follow this rule) are on the previous עמוד, so this line is the second half of a challenge already in progress.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that thought can create a status but only action can remove it is a well-known general principle in the laws of טומאה.

phrases.english: [they] go down into impurity by means of thought,
phrases.notes: This continues the quote that started on 13b about all vessels.

phrases.english: but they do not come up from their impurity
except through a change made by action.
Action takes out of [a status made by] action
and out of [a status made by] thought.
Thought does not take out

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִיַּד מַעֲשֶׂה וְלֹא מִיַּד מַחְשָׁבָה.
phrases.english: neither from [a status made by] action nor from [a status made by] thought.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹרְדִין לִידֵי טוּמְאָה בְּמַחְשָׁבָה, וְאֵין עוֹלִין מִטּוּמְאָתָן אֶלָּא בְּשִׁינּוּי מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge opened at the end of 13b.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the רבנן that stalks harvested for food may be used as סכך, which implies that intent removes the handles' susceptibility to טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general rule says thought cannot remove a status, only action can. The רבנן seem to let thought remove it.

steps.title: Suggested distinction: handles are weaker than real vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a possible way out. The rule may apply only to real, significant כלים. Handles exist only to help with food, so maybe thought alone can both create and remove their status.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: these words apply only to vessels, which are significant. But handles, which exist only for the purpose of eating, become [handles] through thought and leave [that status] through thought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a possible defense of the רבנן. It is setting this defense up only to test it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a real כלי has its own importance, so it needs a real action to lose its status. A handle is only a side helper for food, so its status is weaker and thought might be enough to undo it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test)
Which are significant or important
Handles, such as the stalks attached to grain
Goes away or leaves (that status)

phrases.english: And if you will say: these words apply
to vessels, which are significant,
but handles, which are [only] for the purpose of eating —
through thought it is made, and through thought it goes away.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי כֵּלִים דַּחֲשִׁיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible defense against the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between categories (significant כלים versus secondary handles)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule that only action removes a status applies to every item that receives טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe it applies only to significant כלים, while handles can be undone by thought. This is only proposed and is tested next.

steps.title: A משנה shows handles of food needed an action
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה to reject the suggested distinction. Handles of food become טהור when they were בססן on the threshing floor, which is an action. רבי יוסי says they stay טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned: all handles of foods that one made בססן on the threshing floor are pure (and רבי יוסי deems them impure).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to push back against the suggestion from step 2. It is preparing to show that even handles need a real action to lose their status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say the handles become טהור through intent alone. It ties their purity to something done on the threshing floor, called בססן. How strong this proof is depends on what בססן means, which the next step works out.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה (introduces a source used against something)
Handles of foods, such as stalks attached to grain
A word with two possible meanings: untied them, or trampled them
Threshing floor
Deems it able to become impure

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יוסי's dissenting opinion in this משנה becomes the key to explaining אחרים here.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn [in a משנה]:
All handles of foods
that one 'besasan' on the threshing floor
are pure
(and Rabbi Yosei deems them impure).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: כָּל יְדוֹת הָאוֹכָלִין שֶׁבְּסָסָן בַּגּוֹרֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the distinction proposed in step 2 by citing a משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that handles lose their status through thought alone.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה makes the purity of handles depend on an act done at the threshing floor, not on intention.

steps.title: If בססן means trampling, how do the רבנן work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the force of the משנה. If בססן means untying the bundle, there is no problem. But if it means actually trampling, then even handles need a real physical change, and the view of the רבנן is again difficult.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to the one who says בססן means he untied their binding, that is fine. But according to the one who says בססן means he actually trampled them, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the challenge by looking at the two meanings of בססן. Under one meaning the challenge against the רבנן comes back in full force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Untying a bundle does not change the stalks themselves. It only shows that the owner no longer cares about them, which is close to intention, and that fits the רבנן. Trampling physically changes the stalks, so under that reading handles also need a real action, and the רבנן (who seem to rely on intent alone) have no support.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it works well according to...
He untied their binding
Actually, literally
What is there to say? (signals an unresolved difficulty)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the problem is the משנה itself. The problem is only for the opinion that reads בססן as real trampling, because that reading requires a physical action.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says 'besasan' [means]
he untied their binding, it works well.
But according to the one who says:
what is 'besasan'?
he actually trampled them,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״בְּסָסָן״ הִתִּיר אִגּוּדָן, שַׁפִּיר. אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה in step 3 creates a difficulty for the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the רבנן that stalks harvested for food may be used as סכך because the handles' status has been removed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If בססן means physical trampling, then handles too need a real action to lose their status, so intention alone should not be enough.

steps.title: The רבנן's case also involved real trampling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the stalks the רבנן allow as סכך were also actually trampled. Their status was removed by a real action, not by thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is where he actually trampled them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by redefining the case of the רבנן. It is a case with a physical action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the stalks were trampled, a real action has been done, just as the rule in step 1 requires. So the רבנן never relied on intention alone, and the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too (applying the same case to our sugya)

phrases.english: Here too, [it is a case] where he actually trampled them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, שֶׁבְּסָסָן מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן allow the stalks because of intention alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן speak of stalks that were physically trampled, so a real action removed the handles' status.

steps.title: Then why do אחרים still forbid it?
steps.stepSummary: If the stalks were really trampled and the handles lost their status, the גמרא asks why אחרים still forbid using them as סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the reason of אחרים?
steps.whatsHappening: The answer in step 5 creates a new problem. Now the גמרא needs to explain the other side of the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trampling should remove the handles' ability to become טמא, so the stalks are no longer something that receives טומאה, and they should be fine for סכך. So why would אחרים disagree?

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if we accept the previous answer)
Others, a תנא who is cited without his name

phrases.english: If so, what is the reason of אחרים?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי טַעְמַיְיהוּ דַּאֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the consequence of the answer in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of אחרים, who forbid the stalks as סכך.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If trampling removed the handles' status, nothing should stop the stalks from being used as סכך.

steps.title: אחרים follow רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: אחרים agree with רבי יוסי from the משנה, who holds that handles stay טמא even after trampling. So for them the stalks still receive טומאה and cannot be used as סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they hold like רבי יוסי, as we learned: רבי יוסי deems them impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains אחרים by connecting them to the dissenting opinion of רבי יוסי in the משנה. This answer is challenged right away in the next step, and step 9 defends it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute between the רבנן and אחרים about סכך matches the dispute in the משנה. The רבנן follow the first view (trampled handles are טהור). אחרים follow רבי יוסי (the handles stay טמא), so the stalks still receive טומאה and are not valid as סכך.

keyTerms.meaning: Because they hold in accordance with רבי יוסי
As we learned in a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Only a real action, such as trampling, can remove the טומאה status of food handles. The רבנן speak of trampled stalks, so they allow them as סכך. אחרים forbid them because they follow רבי יוסי, who says trampled handles still receive טומאה.
steps.confusionAlert: The words 'רבי יוסי מטמא' appeared already in step 3. They are repeated here on purpose, to give אחרים a source, not by mistake.

phrases.english: Because they hold like Rabbi Yosei.
As we learned: Rabbi Yosei deems them impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּאֲמוּר כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי. דִּתְנַן: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 by quoting רבי יוסי from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the opinion to an earlier dispute between תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees that trampling removes the handles' status, so אחרים have no reason to forbid.
steps.terutzMaskana: אחרים follow רבי יוסי, who holds that trampled handles still receive טומאה, so the stalks are invalid as סכך.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The סכך dispute between the רבנן and אחרים mirrors the dispute between the first view and רבי יוסי about trampled food handles.

steps.title: How can the סוכה case be compared to the threshing floor?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the link between אחרים and רבי יוסי. On the threshing floor the straw is still useful, but on a סוכה roof the straw seems to have no use.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of comparison is this?! It makes sense there, on the threshing floor. The reason of רבי יוסי is that the stalks are still useful, as רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: since they are fit for turning the grain over with a pitchfork. But here, on the סוכה, what are they useful for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave, that אחרים follow רבי יוסי. It asks how the threshing-floor case can be compared to straw used for סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי keeps the stalks טמא only because they still serve the farmer: they help him turn over the grain with a pitchfork. Straw that is meant only to be a סוכה roof seems to have no such use. So the reason behind רבי יוסי's view does not seem to carry over to the סוכה case.

keyTerms.meaning: "What is this?!" An expression of surprise that challenges a comparison
"Granted / It makes sense". Accepts one case in order to set up a challenge on the other
It is fit / useful (for something)
Since / because
A pitchfork used to turn over grain on the threshing floor

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is rejecting רבי יוסי himself. It accepts his view on the threshing floor. It only questions whether his reason fits the סוכה case.

phrases.english: What is this (comparison)?!
Granted, there (on the threshing floor)
the reason of Rabbi Yosi
is that they are useful, in line with Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish
phrases.notes: Lakish here is a family name; he is also called ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: as Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
since they are fit for turning (the grain) over with a pitchfork.
phrases.notes: The straw keeps the kernels from falling through the prongs.

phrases.english: But here (on the sukkah), what are they useful for?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאי?! בִּשְׁלָמָא הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 7, which said that אחרים follow רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between אחרים (stalks used as סכך) and רבי יוסי (handles on the threshing floor).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's reason is that the straw is still useful. That reason seems missing when the straw is used only as a סוכה roof.

steps.title: The stalks are useful when taking down the סוכה roof
steps.stepSummary: The stalks are useful when the סכך is taken apart, because you can hold the grain by its stalks. So they still count as handles, and אחרים can follow רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are useful for when he takes the roof apart, to hold the grain by its stalks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It finds a real use for the stalks even in a סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the person later dismantles the סכך, he will pick up the grain by grabbing its stalks. So the stalks still work as handles for the food. Because of that, רבי יוסי's reasoning does apply here, and אחרים forbid them as סכך because they can still receive טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes apart / dismantles (the סכך)
To grasp / to hold
Their stalks

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי (and אחרים), a stalk stays a "handle" that can receive טומאה as long as it still has a real use for the food. That is true on the threshing floor (pitchfork) and on the סוכה (holding the grain when taking the roof down).

phrases.english: They are useful for when he dismantles (the sukkah roof)
to hold them (the grain) by their stalks.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַזְיָא לְכִי סָתַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a parallel use, so the reason of רבי יוסי applies to the סוכה case too.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Straw on a סוכה roof has no use for the grain, so רבי יוסי's reason should not apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: The stalks are useful when the roof is taken down, as a way to hold the grain. So they remain handles and can receive טומאה.

steps.title: Returning to the משנה about handles on the threshing floor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again the משנה about handles of food that were בססן on the threshing floor, so that it can now study it on its own terms.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the matter itself: All handles of food that one made בססן on the threshing floor are טהור, and רבי יוסי says they can become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new discussion. It repeats the משנה quoted earlier so that it can now explain that משנה directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the משנה was used as a tool to explain the סכך dispute. Now the גמרא turns to the משנה itself, and especially to the unclear word בססן. This repetition is a real new start, not just a copy.

keyTerms.meaning: "The matter itself". The גמרא returns to examine a source it quoted earlier
Handles of food (stalks attached to the produce)
Threshing floor
Considers it able to become טמא

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself:
All handles of food
that one "besasan" on the threshing floor
are pure (cannot become impure),
and Rabbi Yosi deems them susceptible to impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, כָּל יְדוֹת הָאוֹכָלִין שֶׁבְּסָסָן בַּגּוֹרֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion of the משנה first quoted in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Handles of food that were בססן on the threshing floor are טהור according to the רבנן. רבי יוסי says they can become טמא.

steps.title: What does the word בססן mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the word בססן in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does בססן mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about one unclear word in the משנה. This prepares the dispute that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, in step 4, we saw that the meaning of this word matters a lot. If it means real trampling, the stalks went through a physical action. If it means only untying, nothing much happened to them.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (a request for a definition)
An unclear word in the משנה: either "trampled them" or "untied them"
To trample (the root that the word seems to come from)

phrases.english: What does "besasan" mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״בְּסָסָן״?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the משנה quoted in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact meaning of the word בססן.

steps.title: Two views: real trampling or untying the bundle
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says בססן means real trampling. רבי אלעזר says it means untying the bundle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It means really trampling them. רבי אלעזר says: It means he untied their bundle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different answers to the question about the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, the stalks went through a strong physical action. According to רבי אלעזר, the farmer only untied the bundles, which is a much smaller change. This difference sets up the next question about רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally / actually
Untied / loosened
Their bundle / binding

steps.confusionAlert: The printed text has "רבי (אליעזר)" in parentheses. The accepted reading, used by the Sefaria translation, is רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: It means actually trampling them.
Rabbi (Elazar) says: He untied their binding.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the name in round brackets, רבי אליעזר, but the corrected wording reads it as רבי אלעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: בְּסָסָן מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן: actual trampling. רבי אלעזר: untying the bundle.

steps.title: According to רבי יוחנן, why does רבי יוסי say impure?
steps.stepSummary: If בססן only means untying, it makes sense that רבי יוסי still says טמא. But if it means real trampling, why would רבי יוסי still say the stalks can become טמא?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to רבי אלעזר, who said that בססן means he untied the bundle. That is why רבי יוסי says they can become טמא. But according to רבי יוחנן, who said it means real trampling, why does רבי יוסי say they can become טמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי's view, but only according to רבי יוחנן's reading of the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Untying a bundle is a small act, so it is easy to see why רבי יוסי says the stalks are still handles. Trampling is a strong act that should end their role as handles. So under רבי יוחנן, רבי יוסי's view needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: "That is why" (the case fits the opinion)
But (introduces the difficult side)
Why?

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi (Elazar),
who said "besasan" means he untied their binding,
that is why Rabbi Yosi deems them susceptible to impurity.
But according to Rabbi Yochanan,
who said it means actual trampling,
why does Rabbi Yosi deem them susceptible to impurity?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי (אֱלִיעֶזֶר), דְּאָמַר ״בְּסָסָן״ — הִתִּיר אַגְדָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the dispute of step 12 to question רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's ruling of טמא, according to רבי יוחנן's reading of בססן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Real trampling is a strong action that should cancel the stalks' role as handles, so they should be טהור.

steps.title: The stalks still help turn the grain with a pitchfork
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש explains that even trampled stalks are still useful, because they help turn the grain over with a pitchfork. So they remain handles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: Since they are fit for turning the grain over with a pitchfork.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with the statement of רבי שמעון בן לקיש. This is the original source of the reason quoted earlier in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after trampling, the straw still serves the grain. It keeps the kernels together so they do not fall through the pitchfork's prongs. Because the stalks are still useful to the food, רבי יוסי says they remain handles and can become טמא, even according to רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, also called רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
Fit / suitable
To turn them over

steps.whatToRemember: The key idea of this whole section is usefulness. Stalks keep the status of "handles" that can receive טומאה as long as they still serve the food. On the threshing floor that use is the pitchfork; on the סוכה it is holding the grain when taking the roof down.
steps.whyThisMatters: This statement is the basis for step 8: the entire comparison between אחרים and רבי יוסי rests on the idea of continued usefulness.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Since they are fit for turning (the grain) over with a pitchfork.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: הוֹאִיל וּרְאוּיוֹת לְהוֹפְכָן בְּעֶתֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Continued usefulness keeps the handle status even after a physical action.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Real trampling should end the stalks' status as handles.
steps.terutzMaskana: The trampled stalks still help turn the grain with a pitchfork, so for רבי יוסי they remain handles that can become טמא.

steps.title: The prayers of the righteous are like a pitchfork
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that the prayer of צדיקים is like a pitchfork (עתר). Just as a pitchfork turns grain over, their prayer turns הקדוש ברוך הוא from harshness to mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי (אלעזר) said: Why is the prayer of the צדיקים compared to a pitchfork? To teach you: just as this pitchfork turns the grain over on the threshing floor from place to place, so too the prayer of the צדיקים turns the mind of הקדוש ברוך הוא from the attribute of harshness to the attribute of mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: The previous step mentioned a pitchfork (עתר), so the גמרא adds a short aggadic teaching that uses the same word. This is a side point, not part of the halachic discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עתר (pitchfork) sounds like the word for prayer, as in ויעתר יצחק (יצחק prayed). רבי אלעזר explains the comparison: a pitchfork flips grain from one spot to another, and the prayer of צדיקים 'flips' ה׳'s judgment from מדת אכזריות (harshness) to מדת רחמנות (mercy).

keyTerms.meaning: A pitchfork. Here it is also connected to the word for prayer (וַיֶּעְתַּר)
Righteous people
Turns over, flips
The attribute of harshness or strict judgment
The attribute of mercy

steps.confusionAlert: The text prints the name as (אליעזר) in parentheses. That is a printer's note showing a textual question. The accepted reading is רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: Rabbi (Elazar) said:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the name in round brackets, רבי אליעזר, but the corrected wording reads it as רבי אלעזר.

phrases.aramaic: לָמָּה נִמְשְׁלָה תְּפִלָּתָן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים כְּעֶתֶר
phrases.english: Why is the prayer of the righteous compared to a pitchfork?
phrases.notes: This is based on the verse 'וַיֶּעְתַּר יִצְחָק' (בראשית 25:21).

phrases.english: To tell you:

phrases.aramaic: מָה עֶתֶר זֶה מְהַפֵּךְ אֶת הַתְּבוּאָה
phrases.english: Just as this pitchfork turns over the grain
on the threshing floor, from place to place,
so too the prayer of the righteous turns over
the mind of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
from the attribute of harshness to the attribute of mercy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי (אֱלִיעֶזֶר): לָמָּה נִמְשְׁלָה תְּפִלָּתָן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים כְּעֶתֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching linked by the word עתר (pitchfork), which appeared in ריש לקיש's answer in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prayer of צדיקים turns הקדוש ברוך הוא from strict judgment to mercy, just as a pitchfork turns grain over.

steps.title: New משנה: may a סוכה be roofed with boards?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה allows roofing a סוכה with boards, and רבי מאיר forbids it. If someone put one board four טפחים wide on the סוכה, the סוכה is still כשר, but he may not sleep under that board.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may roof a סוכה with boards; these are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי מאיר forbids it. If one put on it a board that is four טפחים wide, the סוכה is כשרה, as long as he does not sleep under the board.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings an argument about using boards (נסרים) as סכך, and then a rule about one wide board.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Boards are made from wood that grew from the ground and cannot become טמא, so they look like normal סכך. Even so, רבי מאיר forbids them, and the גמרא will explain why. The last part says one wide board does not ruin the whole סוכה, but he may not sleep under it. Later, in step 22, the גמרא says that according to רב this last rule follows רבי מאיר only.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the abbreviation is מַתְנִי׳)
One may put on סכך (roof the סוכה)
Boards, planks
Handbreadths, a unit of measure
As long as, provided that

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה starts the discussion of boards as סכך and of the 'ceiling decree' (גזירת תקרה). That decree is a key idea in the laws of סכך.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One may roof the sukkah with boards,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda,
and Rabbi Meir forbids it.
If one put on it a board
that is four handbreadths wide,
the sukkah is kosher,
as long as he does not sleep under it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מְסַכְּכִין בִּנְסָרִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It is not connected to the previous topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה allows סכך made of boards and רבי מאיר forbids it. One board four טפחים wide does not make the סוכה פסול, but one may not sleep under it.

steps.title: רב: the argument is about wide boards
steps.stepSummary: רב says the argument is about boards four טפחים wide. רבי מאיר holds of גזירת תקרה (the ceiling decree), and רבי יהודה does not. Narrow boards are כשר according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב said: The argument is about boards that are four טפחים wide. רבי מאיר holds of גזירת תקרה, and רבי יהודה does not hold of גזירת תקרה. But with boards that are not four טפחים wide, everyone agrees the סוכה is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה. רב tells us exactly which boards the two תנאים argue about, and why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Boards four טפחים wide look like the ceiling of a house. רבי מאיר says the חכמים made a גזירה against them, because if they were allowed, someone might sit under his own house roof and think it is a סוכה. רבי יהודה does not accept this גזירה. Narrow boards do not look like a ceiling, so no one forbids them.

keyTerms.meaning: The גמרא's discussion (the abbreviation is גְּמָ׳)
An argument or dispute
The ceiling decree: a rabbinic rule forbidding סכך that looks like a house ceiling
He holds of it / he does not hold of it
Everyone agrees

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rav said:
The argument is about boards that are four handbreadths wide,

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר אִית לֵיהּ גְּזֵרַת תִּקְרָה,
phrases.english: because Rabbi Meir holds of the ceiling decree,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לֵית לֵיהּ גְּזֵרַת תִּקְרָה.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda does not hold of the ceiling decree.
But with boards that are not four handbreadths wide,
everyone agrees the sukkah is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מַחְלוֹקֶת בִּנְסָרִין שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which case the משנה's argument is about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is only about boards four טפחים wide, and it depends on גזירת תקרה. Narrow boards are כשר according to everyone.

steps.title: שמואל: the argument is about narrow boards
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב. He says the argument is about boards less than four טפחים wide. Boards four wide are פסול according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: The argument is about boards that are not four טפחים wide. But if they are four טפחים wide, everyone agrees the סוכה is פסולה.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the opposite reading of the משנה. He moves the argument from wide boards to narrow boards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, everyone (even רבי יהודה) agrees that wide boards are פסול. So the argument must be about narrow boards. This makes it harder to understand why רבי מאיר would forbid them, and the גמרא is about to ask exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: Unfit, not valid as a סוכה
That do not have (the width)

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
The argument is about boards that are not four handbreadths wide,
but if they are four handbreadths wide,
everyone agrees the sukkah is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: בְּשֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן אַרְבָּעָה מַחֲלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading from רב's in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is about narrow boards. Boards four טפחים wide are פסול according to everyone.

steps.title: Challenge to שמואל: very narrow boards are just like reeds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל. If the argument covers all boards narrower than four טפחים, it includes boards narrower than three. Those are just like reeds, so why would רבי מאיר forbid them?
steps.simpleTranslation: If the boards are not four handbreadths wide, and even less than three, aren't they just ordinary reeds?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's reading. It asks how רבי מאיר could forbid boards that are so thin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, the argument is about boards under four טפחים, which seems to include boards under three. A board that thin is no different from a reed, and reeds are normal, כשר סכך. So it seems very strange for רבי מאיר to forbid them. The גמרא needs an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than three (טפחים)
Reeds, which are standard כשר סכך
Merely, just ordinary
They are

phrases.english: If they are not four handbreadths wide,
and even less than three,
aren't they just ordinary reeds?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בָּהֶן אַרְבָּעָה, וַאֲפִילּוּ פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה, הָא קָנִים בְּעָלְמָא נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's reading from Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that רבי מאיר forbids even narrow boards
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Boards narrower than three טפחים are just like reeds, which are כשר סכך. So רבי מאיר should have no reason to forbid them.

steps.title: רב פפא explains that שמואל means boards three to four wide
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא defends שמואל. Boards four or more wide are פסול according to everyone, and boards under three are כשר according to everyone. The argument is only about boards three to four wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is what שמואל means. If the boards are four טפחים wide, everyone agrees the סוכה is פסול. If they are less than three, everyone agrees it is כשר. Why? Because they are just like reeds. The argument is about boards from three to four. One opinion holds that since they are not big enough to count as a 'place', we do not make a decree. The other opinion holds that since they are too wide for לבוד, we do make a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question it just asked against שמואל. רב פפא narrows שמואל's words so that the argument only covers boards between three and four טפחים wide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that boards under three are just reeds, so why would רבי מאיר forbid them? רב פפא agrees that boards under three are כשר according to everyone. רבי יהודה says boards of three to four are too small to be a real 'place', so he makes no גזירה. רבי מאיר says they are already too wide for לבוד, so he does make a גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means. Used to reinterpret an earlier statement.
Just ordinary reeds, meaning normal כשר סכך
The size that counts as a real 'place', which is four טפחים
The rule that a gap or piece less than three טפחים is treated as joined, as if it is not there separately
We make a decree, a rabbinic safeguard

steps.confusionAlert: Three is not the same as four here. Three טפחים is the limit for לבוד. Four טפחים is the size of a real 'place' (שיעור מקום). The argument sits in the space between these two numbers.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, שמואל holds: under three is כשר according to everyone, four or more is פסול according to everyone, and only three to four is the argument. רבי מאיר makes a גזירה there, and רבי יהודה does not.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: This is what he (Shmuel) means:
If they have four (handbreadths of width)
everyone agrees it is unfit.
If less than three, everyone agrees it is fit.
What is the reason? They are merely reeds.
Where they disagree is from three to four.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּלֵיתַנְהוּ שִׁיעוּר מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: One master holds: since they are not the size of a 'place',
we do not make a decree.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּנָפְקִי לְהוּ מִתּוֹרַת לָבוּד,
phrases.english: And the other master holds: since they have left the category of lavud,
we do make a decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19 against שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation. It narrows the range of the argument.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought שמואל meant that every board under four is in the argument, including boards under three.
steps.terutzMaskana: Boards under three are כשר according to everyone. The argument is only about boards of three to four, and it depends on whether to make a גזירה.

steps.title: Challenge to רב from the rule against sleeping under the board
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says you may not sleep under a four-טפח board. That fits שמואל, who holds such a board is פסול according to everyone. But according to רב, רבי יהודה permits four-טפח boards, so why can't one sleep under it?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: If he put a board four טפחים wide on the סוכה, the סוכה is כשר, but he may not sleep under it. This works well for שמואל. He said the argument is about boards narrower than four, but a board of four is פסול according to everyone. That is why one may not sleep under it. But רב said the argument is about boards of four, and narrower boards are כשר according to everyone. So according to רבי יהודה, why may he not sleep under it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה to attack רב. The rule against sleeping under the board makes sense for שמואל, but it seems to clash with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, a four-טפח board is פסול סכך for everyone, so sleeping under it is like sleeping without valid סכך. According to רב, a four-טפח board is exactly what רבי יהודה permits. So for רבי יהודה it should be fine to sleep under it.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה
Granted, this works well for one view
But, used for the view that has a problem
Why?

phrases.english: We learned: If he placed upon it a board
that is four handbreadths wide, it is fit,
provided he does not sleep under it.
Granted, according to Shmuel, who said
the dispute is where they do not have four,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יֵשׁ בָּהֶן אַרְבָּעָה דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל פְּסוּלָה,
phrases.english: but where they have four, everyone agrees it is unfit,
that is why he may not sleep under it.
But according to Rav, who said
the dispute is where they have four,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין בָּהֶן אַרְבָּעָה דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרָה,
phrases.english: but where they do not have four, everyone agrees it is fit,

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַמַּאי לֹא יִישַׁן תַּחְתָּיו?
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Yehuda, why may he not sleep under it?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: נָתַן עָלֶיהָ נֶסֶר שֶׁהוּא רָחָב אַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With שמואל now defended, the גמרא turns to test רב against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that רבי יהודה permits boards four טפחים wide
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids sleeping under a four-טפח board, which implies the board is פסול. According to רב, רבי יהודה holds such a board is כשר, so the rule would not fit רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The sleeping rule follows רבי מאיר only
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the end of the משנה is not agreed by everyone. It follows רבי מאיר, so it is no problem for רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think this rule is agreed by everyone? The last part of the משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. The rule against sleeping under the board was never meant to follow רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the last clause of the משנה is everyone's opinion. The answer is that it is only רבי מאיר's view, since he forbids four-טפח boards. רבי יהודה would allow sleeping under it, so there is no proof against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think...? Introduces rejecting a wrong assumption.
The latter clause of a משנה
We have come to (another opinion)

phrases.english: Do you think it is the view of everyone?
In the latter clause we have come to Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 21 against רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the clause to one תנא. The end of the משנה follows רבי מאיר alone.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sleeping rule was thought to be agreed by both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sleeping rule is רבי מאיר's view only, so רב's understanding of רבי יהודה still stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: After this step, both רב and שמואל can explain the משנה. Neither view has been disproven yet.

steps.title: A new source opens: two sheets combine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new proof from a ברייתא that says two sheets combine. The rest of the proof comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Two sheets combine.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is bringing a new source to test רב and שמואל again, and the full argument continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sheets spread over the סכך join together to reach four טפחים, the size of פסול סכך that can make the סוכה פסול. The גמרא will soon compare this to boards to see which view the ברייתא supports.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. Introduces a source brought as a proof.
Sheets (cloths), which are פסול סכך
Combine, adding together to reach a measurement

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Two sheets combine (to make four handbreadths).

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שְׁנֵי סְדִינִין מִצְטָרְפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה was rejected, the גמרא brings a new source from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Deciding between רב and שמואל on which board widths are in the argument
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: two sheets combine to make four טפחים. The rest is quoted on the next עמוד.
